hero.headline: Turn enterprise archives into private, governed intelligence.
hero.body: iDocHive digitizes, governs, searches, and applies private AI to sensitive documents inside your approved environment. Your documents, models, keys, prompts, responses, and audit records remain under your control.

end.answer: Payment terms follow Clause 12.4 of Contract ALS-09 and Variation Order VO-118.
end.audit: Audit event written · approved_by records officer

problem.headline: Your most valuable knowledge is trapped in documents.
problem.body: Decades of knowledge sit across paper archives, scans, PDFs, shared drives, and legacy systems. Employees struggle to find trusted answers. Manual processing raises cost. Public AI introduces data-control concerns. iDocHive creates one governed path from document intake to accountable intelligence.

transform.headline: Paper to data. Data to information. Information to intelligence.

stages.title: Paper
stages.text: Scan and ingest physical records, digital files, and approved system captures. Preserve the original source.

stages.title: Data
stages.text: Run OCR, detect type, extract fields and tables, and route low-confidence results for human review.

stages.title: Information
stages.text: Classify, apply retention and access rules, index content, and support keyword, semantic, and hybrid search.

stages.title: Intelligence
stages.text: Ask questions across authorized content, return citations, review high-impact outputs, and act with evidence.

how.headline: From intake to accountable answers
how.body: The operational sequence stays inside your boundary: import, encrypt, process, govern, retrieve, cite, approve, and record.

governance.headline: AI remains inside your rules.
governance.body: Every query respects document permissions. Every answer points to source evidence. Controlled outputs wait for human approval. Every access, inference, and decision creates an audit event.

cards.title: Permission-aware retrieval
cards.text: RBAC is enforced in the API and retrieval layers, not only in the interface. Unauthorized collections never enter the model context.

cards.title: Source validation
cards.text: Answers include citations to original passages. Users can inspect the evidence before they act.

cards.title: Human approval
cards.text: High-impact outputs remain in pending_review until an authorized person approves, rejects, or requests changes.

cards.title: Complete audit evidence
cards.text: The trail links the user, sources, model version, prompt policy, response, reviewer, and decision.

deployment.headline: Built for infrastructure you control.
deployment.body: There is no public multi-tenant SaaS edition. Choose the boundary that matches the information class.

architecture.headline: A product layer on infrastructure you already govern
architecture.body: The marketing site is not the product. The product application uses Vue 3 with Inertia, Laravel, and a PostgreSQL + pgvector data layer inside your environment.

layers.title: Access
layers.text: Web experience, search, document viewer, workflow inbox, and administration. Product UI: Vue 3 with Inertia.

layers.title: Application and policy
layers.text: Laravel APIs, business rules, permissions, workflow controls, and audit enforcement.

layers.title: Isolated AI inference
layers.text: OCR gateway, LangGraph workflows, and vLLM behind an internal model gateway. No public AI API required.

layers.title: Data: PostgreSQL + pgvector
layers.text: PostgreSQL is the customer-controlled system of record. pgvector stores embeddings beside governed metadata so retrieval stays inside the same security boundary.

layers.title: Security and observability
layers.text: Identity provider, SIEM, backup, signed offline updates, metrics, logs, and traces.

useCases.headline: Where governed document intelligence is required

items.title: Government archive intelligence
items.problem: Historical records remain paper, poorly scanned, or locked in departmental stores.
items.workflow: Digitize, classify, apply access rules, and provide permission-aware search with private AI assistance.
items.result: Authorized staff retrieve trusted records without exposing restricted collections.
items.control: Record-level permissions and complete audit history

items.title: Contract intelligence
items.problem: Obligations, renewals, and version differences are found by hand.
items.workflow: Extract parties, dates, terms, and risks while preserving source evidence.
items.result: Legal and commercial teams compare versions with citations.

items.title: Construction and project document control
items.problem: Drawings, variations, transmittals, and handover packs fragment across contractors.
items.workflow: Register, version, route approvals, and retrieve related project records.
items.result: Document controllers keep one governed project memory.

items.title: Policy and procedure assistant
items.problem: Staff cannot find the current approved circular or SOP.
items.workflow: Ask questions only over authorized, current policy collections.
items.result: Answers cite the approved source instead of informal copies.

items.title: Controlled correspondence
items.problem: Incoming letters miss owners, deadlines, and a durable history.
items.workflow: Capture, classify, assign, monitor, and retain correspondence.
items.result: Case owners see status, evidence, and decisions in one trail.

items.title: Museum and provenance records
items.problem: Appraisal, collection, and provenance files are sensitive and hard to search.
items.workflow: Govern specialist records with restricted access and cited research answers.
items.result: Curators work from authorized evidence, not detached copies.

compare.headline: Why organizations choose a governed intelligence layer
compare.body: The difference is the combined lifecycle — capture, system of record, permission-aware retrieval, and private AI with human approval — inside infrastructure you control.

rows.focus: iDocHive adds document intelligence, hybrid retrieval, structured extraction, and governed AI workflows.
Extraction is only the start. Permissions, metadata, search, retention, and organizational use continue after the text is captured.
Documents, models, prompts, responses, keys, and logs remain inside the approved customer boundary.
Search sits on top of ingestion, OCR, governance, workflows, and source-grounded generation.

final.headline: Start with one document collection and one measurable outcome.
final.body: Define the use case, security boundary, document profile, and success measures before committing to enterprise rollout.
